title: prd-clarity-checkpoint-playbook-for-rolling-scope-variants
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: create a pragmatic, repeatable playbook that converts ambiguous PRD scope-changes into a set of concrete cross-team acceptance checkpoints and sign-off artifacts. This ticket defines the lanes, owners, gating criteria, and example templates that PMs will use when a PRD introduces rolling/variant scope (eg. staged structured-output, model-variant fallbacks, regional feature rollouts).

Background: Recent PRD changes for structured-output v2 introduced vague acceptance language causing delays: engineering and legal waited on explicit SLOs and data residency clauses; design had open UX failure-cases. We need a lighter-weight, enforceable path that reduces review friction while preserving risk controls.

Scope: produce a playbook + one-page checklist template + canonical example for structured-output changes. The deliverables below target the first 8-week runway: a) playbook doc, b) change checklist template, c) sample signed-off PRD (annotated), d) automated checklist in PR description template.

Acceptance lanes (one-line overview):
- Engineering lane: perf/regression SLOs, KV cache compatibility, canary traffic window, rollback criteria, benchmark artifacts.
- Design lane: interaction flows for degraded outputs, schema examples, failure messages, accessibility checks.
- Legal lane: data residency mapping, export-control review (if model/data crosses regions), contract clause stub for customers.
- Security lane: KMS integration checklist, audit log capture path, RBAC scope changes.

Concrete sign-off artifacts required per lane:
- Engineering: benchmark report link + perf gating table (p50/p95 token latency; memory delta; cost per 1k tokens) + one PR for the runtime changes + canary run log.
- Design: annotated prototype with 3 user scenarios + acceptance QA script executed by design QA.
- Legal: short memo (1 page) listing policy impact + explicit clause language for contracts + sign-off from Legal owner.
- Security: short checklist confirming KMS and audit coverage + security approver signature.

Gating rules (how a checkpoint works):
1) PM publishes PRD change and selects lanes affected. 2) Each lane owner has 5 business days to respond with 'accept', 'request changes', or 'block'. 3) If any lane blocks, PM opens a remediation sub-issue and coordinates triage. 4) If lanes accept with minor changes, PM records conditional acceptance and tracks follow-ups in the release notes.

Rollback policy: a default automatic rollback if canary latency regressions exceed 15% p95 or error rate increases > 1% absolute over baseline within the first 24h of rollout. The PM must coordinate emergency rollback runbook with Eng SRE.

Next steps/deliverables:
- Draft playbook (owner: Miguel Rivera) by 2026-03-14 (this ticket).
- One-page checklist template (owner: Asha Patel) by 2026-03-18.
- Sample annotated PRD for structured-output (owner: Miguel Rivera) by 2026-03-22.
- PR description automation in the repo templates (owner: ENG-51234) by 2026-03-29.

Metrics of success: reduction in PRD acceptance cycle time from review to sign-off by 40% on sample cohort; fewer emergency rollbacks tied to ambiguity; improved clarity in telemetry mapping for rollouts.

Links and artifacts: see links field for draft artifacts and example templates.
